messages.title: Should You Send It Again?
messages.subtitle: The response never arrives. The VM may or may not exist. What does the contract let you do next?
messages.observation: No completion response before the caller’s deadline.
messages.property: One logical CreateVM operation must not create two VMs.
messages.weakContract: No documented repeat protection; no additional outcome evidence.
messages.strongContract: Compatible repeats carrying P are one logical operation; the receiver will not create a second VM for P within its defined scope.
messages.step.review.title: The code looks reasonable
messages.step.review.lead: The caller retries when the completion response does not arrive. Read the code, then decide whether that is safe.
messages.step.review.question: Is the deadline alone enough to justify another CreateVM request?
messages.step.review.feedback: Hold that answer. First separate the caller’s observation from the remote effect.
messages.step.evidence.title: What did the caller observe?
messages.step.evidence.lead: The caller received no completion response before its deadline. In this teaching model, transport cannot establish that the request definitely never left.
messages.step.evidence.question: Which claim does that observation establish?
messages.step.evidence.feedback: The observation establishes only that no completion response arrived in time. It does not, by itself, establish either remote outcome.
messages.step.worlds.title: Two possible worlds
messages.step.worlds.lead: These are representative executions, not an exhaustive list. The caller sees the same thing in both.
messages.worlds.aria: Two representative executions compatible with the same observation
messages.worlds.aDescription: The request may not have produced an external effect.
messages.worlds.bDescription: The effect occurred, but its completion response is unavailable.
messages.step.property.title: Name the property
messages.step.property.lead: For this case, safety takes priority when an unprotected repeat cannot be justified.
messages.step.property.label: The property
messages.step.property.explanation: Automatic progress is desirable too, but the current contract may leave the operation unresolved. That is not the same as failed.
messages.step.weak-contract.title: Test the weak contract
messages.step.weak-contract.label: Contract A · No repeat protection
messages.step.weak-contract.lead: There is no documented guarantee that a repeat represents the same logical operation, and there is no additional outcome evidence.
messages.step.weak-contract.feedback: This execution is allowed by Contract A and violates the stated property. The contract does not justify an unprotected independent repeat here.
messages.step.strong-contract.title: Change the contract, not the failure
messages.step.strong-contract.label: Contract B · Same logical operation
messages.step.strong-contract.lead: Keep the same failure, observation, representative worlds, and property. Change only the receiver contract.
messages.step.strong-contract.explanation: The caller assigns identity P before A1. A compatible repeat with P represents the same logical operation. Within the receiver’s defined scope, it will not create a second VM for P. Incompatible reuse is rejected or explicitly handled.
messages.step.strong-contract.insight: The failure did not change. The justified action changed because the contract changed.
messages.step.scope-challenge.title: The identity boundary
messages.step.scope-challenge.lead: The receiver protects a logical operation identified by P. Now the caller sends A1(P) and then A2(Q).
messages.step.scope-challenge.question: Does protection for P prevent two VMs?
messages.step.scope-challenge.feedback: No. The receiver can honor its contract for each identity while P and Q create two VMs. The caller lost identity continuity.
messages.step.positive-control.title: Protection can permit progress
messages.step.positive-control.lead: Repeat protection should still allow a legitimate completion path.
messages.step.positive-control.aria: Same identity makes progress without a second VM
messages.step.positive-control.insight: Safety does not require rejecting every repeat.
messages.step.negative-control.title: A repeat can be safe
messages.step.negative-control.lead: Consider a different operation under an explicit repeat-safe contract:
messages.step.negative-control.label: Set desired state
messages.step.negative-control.explanation: If repeating this request simply reasserts the same desired state, the same network ambiguity can permit a repeat. The contract and property, not the timeout alone, determine the action.
messages.step.transfer.title: Try another domain
messages.step.transfer.lead: Transfer the reasoning to Charge(request_id=P, amount=100) under a same-logical-operation repeat contract.
messages.step.transfer.question: Which sequence preserves the same logical identity?
messages.step.transfer.feedback: P → P is a compatible repeat within the stated contract. P → Q can represent another charge. The identity must survive the caller’s own failure and retry path.
messages.step.remaining.title: What can still fail?
messages.step.remaining.lead: Contract B closes this counterexample only within its scope. It does not settle every failure.
messages.remaining.lost.title: Lost P after a crash
messages.remaining.lost.text: A new identity may create another VM.
messages.remaining.reuse.title: Incompatible reuse
messages.remaining.reuse.text: The receiver must define and handle changed specs.
messages.remaining.retention.title: Retention window
messages.remaining.retention.text: Protection may expire before a late retry.
messages.remaining.concurrent.title: Hidden retries and concurrency
messages.remaining.concurrent.text: SDKs, proxies, and overlapping attempts must honor identity continuity.
messages.remaining.reconcile.title: Reconciliation evidence
messages.remaining.reconcile.text: Eventually consistent NOT_FOUND need not prove no effect occurred.
messages.step.recap.title: The six questions
messages.step.recap.lead: Use these six questions whenever a remote result is uncertain.
messages.recap.2: What execution does the current contract still allow?
messages.recap.5: Can the bad execution still occur?
messages.step.recap.insight: Same observation. Different contract. Different justified action.
messages.option.vmNotCreated: The VM definitely was not created
messages.option.scopeNo: No, Q is another logical operation
messages.option.challengeUnresolved: Keep the operation unresolved; seek stronger evidence or contract
messages.option.challengeAssume: Assume the VM was not created
messages.challenge.title: What should the caller do?
messages.challenge.intro: You have the code, the observation, the property, and Contract A.
messages.challenge.question: Given the evidence and contract, which action is safe?
messages.challenge.feedback: Contract A permits A1 to create a VM and A2 to create another. The safe immediate choice under this property is to keep the operation unresolved while seeking a stronger contract or evidence. A timeout does not prove failure.
messages.deepDive.title: Where does the retry guarantee end?
messages.deepDive.section1.title: What the caller actually knows
messages.deepDive.section1.body: In this teaching model, the caller did not receive a completion response before its deadline. The transport cannot establish that the request definitely never left. That observation alone does not establish whether a VM exists.
messages.deepDive.section2.title: Identity belongs to a logical operation
messages.deepDive.section2.body: An attempt is a transmission. The logical operation is the intended creation. The stronger receiver contract only protects compatible repeats carrying the same identity P. A caller that crashes and loses P, or a hidden SDK that retries under a new identity, can step outside that protection.
messages.deepDive.section3.title: Contract boundaries still matter
messages.deepDive.section3.body: The receiver must define how long it retains P, what counts as a compatible spec, and what happens with concurrent attempts. A NOT_FOUND result from a query may reflect eventual consistency; it does not automatically prove that the original create attempt had no effect. Reconciliation can help, but its evidence is only as strong as the query contract.
